name: Russian Beef Stroganoff
description: Beef stroganoff, named for the wealthy Stroganov merchant family, genuinely reflects French technique adapted with real Russian smetana (sour cream) - real technique cuts the beef against the grain into thin strips, then sears it in small batches so each piece browns in a single layer rather than steaming from overcrowding; real tradition serves it with straw-cut fried potatoes or buckwheat kasha, not egg noodles, which is more an American adaptation.
steps_detailed: Season the beef strips with salt and pepper, and sear in batches in half the butter over high heat, 2-3 minutes per batch, so each piece browns rather than steams - real technique never crowds the pan here.
In the same pan, cook the onion and mushrooms in the remaining butter, 5-6 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir, then add the sour cream, mustard, and tomato paste, and simmer 5 minutes until thickened.
Return the beef and warm through, 2-3 minutes.
Cook the buckwheat groats separately per package directions, and serve the stroganoff over it - real tradition, not egg noodles.

name: Russian Pelmeni
description: Pelmeni, Russia's real meat dumplings, are a genuine winter family tradition, real technique grates the onion rather than chopping it, which keeps the filling genuinely moist and lets it integrate smoothly into the meat rather than leaving large chunks.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and egg with cold water into a smooth, firm dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Mix the beef with the grated onion and pepper - real technique grates rather than chops the onion, which keeps the filling moist.
Roll the dough thin and cut into small rounds, fill each with a small spoonful of filling, and fold and pinch into a sealed dumpling.
Boil in salted water 8-9 minutes until they float and the filling is cooked through.

name: Russian Olivier Salad
description: Olivier salad, a real diced vegetable and mayonnaise salad, is a genuine Russian New Year's staple, real technique dicing everything uniformly small so each bite gets a bit of every ingredient.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peas, green, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

ingredients.ingredient: Peas, green, frozen, cooked, boiled, drained, without salt

steps_detailed: Dice the boiled potato, carrot, and hard-boiled egg uniformly small.
Toss everything together with the peas and mayonnaise.

name: Russian Chicken Kiev
description: Chicken Kiev, a real breaded cutlet wrapped around butter, real technique chilling the butter thoroughly before wrapping so it doesn't melt out during breading and frying.
steps_detailed: Place the chilled butter in the center of the pounded chicken and roll up tightly, sealing the edges completely.
Freeze 15-20 minutes to firm up further.
Dredge in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry at 350F (175C) for 6-8 minutes until deeply golden and cooked through.

name: Russian Blini
description: Blini, real thin yeasted pancakes, are a beloved Russian staple, real technique letting the batter rest and rise before cooking for a genuine light, slightly tangy character.
steps_detailed: Whisk the flour, egg, milk, baking powder, and melted butter into a thin, smooth batter.
Let rest 20-30 minutes.
Cook in a lightly oiled pan, thin like a crepe, 1-2 minutes per side, until lightly golden.

name: Russian Beet and Herring Salad (Shuba-Style)
description: Shuba, a real layered beet and fish salad, is a beloved Russian New Year's dish, real technique layering the ingredients in a specific order so the beet's color bleeds through as the finishing layer.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Fish, sardine, Atlantic, canned in oil, drained solids with bone

ingredients.ingredient: Fish, sardine, Atlantic, canned in oil, drained solids with bone

steps_detailed: Layer the grated potato, flaked fish, and grated beet in a dish, spreading a thin layer of mayonnaise between each.
Chill at least 1 hour before serving, so the beet color bleeds through the top layer.

name: Russian Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with dill and lemon, reflecting Russia's vast river and lake fishing tradition.
steps_detailed: Rub the fish with the dill and lemon juice, and let sit 10 minutes.
Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.

name: Russian Roasted Almonds
description: A simple roasted almond snack, common across Russia.
steps_detailed: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring often, 4-5 minutes, until fragrant.

Add the carrot, potato, and tomatoes, and simmer 30-35 minutes until tender.
